text:
Wyatt Kaiser is playing 20 minutes a night for a Blackhawks team that has won one of its last ten games with him in the lineup, and he wore plenty of it: minus-5 in the 9-2 loss at Carolina on November 7, per Mark Lazerus of The Athletic. After that game, Lazerus reported, the players held a meeting, and Kaiser said the team needs to "ball up" and start winning battles.

The numbers explain why it hurts. At five on five, Chicago gets only 35% of the expected goals (the quality of chances, for and against) with him on the ice, worse than the team without him. Some of that is company: Evolving-Hockey ranked his teammates' impact in the bottom 1% last season. And Chicago has scored 10.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, which usually swings back.

His own production is fine for his role: six points in 18 games, including a goal 57 seconds into the November 2 game against Colorado. Two goals on 15 shots won't last, but a 24-year-old getting these minutes on a rebuilding team has room to grow into them. Our range has him at 17 to 32 points.
headline: Wyatt Kaiser is in the middle of Chicago's slide
